items.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
items.abstract: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure. The model accepts text and image inputs and produces text outputs, was trained on data from over a hundred languages, and is quantized to approximately 4-bit precision for efficient single-GPU inference. Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion. We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.
items.title_ko: 30B 에이전틱 모델 Muse Glimmer 공개 — 온디바이스 4비트 양자화로 Gemma4-31B·Qwen3.6-27B 능가
items.summary: Muse Glimmer는 지각 인코더를 결합한 300억 파라미터 규모의 오픈소스 인과 언어모델로, 소비자용 하드웨어에서 자율 에이전트 작업을 수행하도록 설계됐다. 다단계 추론, 신뢰성 있는 도구 사용, 실패 복구 기능을 하나의 모델에 통합해 클라우드 없이 로컬에서 동작한다. 텍스트와 이미지를 입력받아 텍스트를 출력하며 100개 이상 언어 데이터로 학습됐고, 단일 GPU 추론을 위해 약 4비트로 양자화됐다. 도구 사용, 다단계 계획, 에이전틱 작업 완수 벤치마크에서 **Gemma4-31B와 Qwen3.6-27B를 능가**하는 동급 최고 성능을 보였으며, Apache 2.0 라이선스로 공개됐다.

items.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture
items.abstract: Microsoft researcher and collaborator combine new mathematical ideas with human-directed AI to resolve a central problem in high-dimensional geometry and probability At a glance Fundamental scientific breakthrough: Researchers resolved the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits (KLS) conjecture, a 31-year-old problem widely regarded as one of the central open questions in high-dimensional geometry, with implications for statistics, optimization, algorithms, and computer science. A universal geometric principle: The result establishes a universal geometric principle for log-concave distributions, showing that simple flat cuts can capture their narrowest bottlenecks within a fixed factor, regardless of dimension. Human-AI collaboration: The breakthrough emerged from a human-directed agentic research process in which AI systems explored mathematical possibilities while researchers evaluated, pruned, and redirected the search. Independent confirmation: Multiple independent researchers have validated this research, identifying its central criterion as the key breakthrough, followed by a machine-checked formal verification. For decades, a fundamental question about the difficulty of computing in high-dimensional spaces has resisted proof. New research resolves this question, removing a major theoretical obstacle to understanding the efficiency of randomized algorithms used across science and computing. The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits (KLS) conjecture was proposed in 1995. It asks whether, for a broad class of high-dimensional probability distributions, the best flat or hyperplane cut is always nearly as effective as the best cut of any shape. More precisely, KLS predicts that the two differ by no more than a universal constant, regardless of the number of dimensions. This would establish a dimension-free geometric principle with important consequences for high-dimensional geometry, probability, and theoretical computer science. Because the geometry of these cuts governs how quickly random walks can explore a distribution, KLS also plays a central role in the theory of high-dimensional sampling. Figure 1: An illustration of the KLS Conjecture (simplified) on regular tetrahedron. Since 1995, mathematicians have accumulated evidence that the conjecture was true, but a complete proof remained elusive. Now, two researchers, including Xinzhi Zhang from the Machine Learning and Optimization group at Microsoft Research, have proved the KLS conjecture (opens in new tab) . They have shown that the relationship holds with a fixed bound, regardless of how many dimensions a shape has. Before this work, the best known result (opens in new tab) , established in July 2026, allowed that bound to grow slowly as the number of dimensions increased. This work establishes a fundamental geometric principle: high-dimensional spaces are better behaved than previously known, and the obstacles to navigating them do not grow without bound as dimensions increase. The importance of the KLS conjecture was recognized across the field long before it was resolved. In its 2017-18 Annual Report, the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute (MSRI) (opens in new tab) called it “a central open problem in high-dimensional convex geometry.” The Simons Institute (opens in new tab) described it as “one of the most important open problems in convex geometry.” In the proceedings of the 2022 International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM) (opens in new tab) , Ronen Eldan noted its broad implications for high-dimensional convex and computational geometry. Quanta Magazine (opens in new tab) wrote that KLS “lies at the heart of many questions in statistics and computer science.” Technical details The authors began by improving the July 2026 result in order to make the mathematical bound more precise. Working with AI agents in a structured, human-directed process, they explored more than 100 candidate approaches, many involving lengthy calculations with higher-order tensors. items.title_ko: Microsoft, 31년 난제 KLS 추측 증명 — AI 에이전트가 100개 이상 접근법 탐색해 고차원 기하학 돌파
items.summary: Microsoft Research의 Xinzhi Zhang 등 연구자들이 1995년 제기된 Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits(KLS) 추측을 증명했다. 이 추측은 로그오목 분포에서 가장 좋은 평면 절단이 어떤 형태의 절단과 비교해도 차원과 무관한 고정 상수 이내로 근접함을 주장한다. 기존 2026년 7월 결과는 이 경계가 차원 증가에 따라 서서히 커지는 것을 허용했으나, 이번 연구는 **고정된 경계**가 성립함을 보였다. 연구진은 AI 에이전트가 고차 텐서 계산을 포함한 100개 이상의 후보 접근법을 탐색하고 인간 연구자가 평가·조정하는 human-directed agentic 방식으로 증명을 완성했으며, 이후 독립적 검증과 기계 검증된 형식 검증을 거쳤다.
items.why_it_matters: KLS 추측은 고차원 샘플링과 무작위 알고리즘의 효율성을 좌우하는 핵심 이론적 장벽으로, 통계·최적화·이론 컴퓨터과학 전반에 영향을 미친다. 이번 증명은 **인간-AI 협업 연구 프로세스**가 수십 년간 풀리지 않던 수학 난제 해결에 실질적으로 기여할 수 있음을 보여주는 사례다.
items.whats_different: 2026년 7월까지의 최선의 결과는 차원이 늘어날수록 경계가 서서히 커지는 것을 허용했지만, 이번 연구는 **차원과 무관한 고정 경계**를 확립해 기존 결과를 넘어섰다.

items.title: Train Qwen3 on AWS Trainium with torchtitan
items.abstract: Using torchtitan on AWS Trainium means using it the way you always have. TorchNeuron registers Trainium as a native PyTorch device, which lets torchtitan use it through standard PyTorch interfaces. You can use these configurations to pre-train from random initialization or fine-tune published weights. You can also customize the model implementation and kernels for your workload. In this post, you train Qwen3 three ways on a single trn2.48xlarge . The first method uses Transformers v5 as a modeling backend in torchtitan. It runs Hub models through AutoModelForCausalLM and reads and writes published safetensors directly. The second method switches to torchtitan’s native Qwen3 by changing config.model_spec . The third adds Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) mixture-of-experts (MoE) kernels from the torchtitan-neuron recipes and then uses torchtitan’s override registry to attach your own kernel. All three configurations use the same torchrun launch pattern and config structure. Prerequisites To follow this walkthrough, use a single trn2.48xlarge with either the AWS Deep Learning AMI for Neuron or a Neuron PyTorch training container. Both environments provide the Neuron driver, runtime, and compiler required to train on Trainium. Before you install torchtitan-neuron , check whether your environment already includes it. The following command prints the installed version and package path: python3 -c "import torchtitan, torchtitan_neuron; print(torchtitan.__version__, torchtitan_neuron.__file__)" This walkthrough uses the versions in the following table. To reproduce the examples, pin these versions. The Transformers v5 integration and Trainium-specific override modules can change between torchtitan releases. Component Version Instance trn2.48xlarge, 16 Trainium2 accelerators, 128 physical NeuronCores Logical NeuronCores 64 at LNC=2 torch, torch_neuronx 2.14.0, 2.14.3 transformers 5.16.0 torchtitan-neuron release-2.33 (0.2.2+neuron.1) When torch_neuronx is installed, TorchNeuron registers Trainium as the neuron device and torchtitan detects it at startup. In eager mode, Neuron compiles operations as they execute. With torch.compile , Neuron compiles the captured graph. This same launch pattern works across all three configurations. For the versions used in this walkthrough, install torchtitan-neuron and torchtitan’s remaining dependencies with --no-deps to preserve the Neuron build of torch: git clone https://github.com/aws-neuron/torchtitan-neuron cd torchtitan-neuron pip install -r requirements.txt Before you start training, get the Qwen3 model artifacts from Hugging Face Hub. Store them in a local directory that you can pass to the training config: hf download Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 \ --local-dir "$PWD/assets/hf/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507" Each training configuration is a Python config function. The three examples start from a base config that you update for each step. Train with Hugging Face Transformers v5 In the first configuration, Transformers v5 builds Qwen3 through AutoModelForCausalLM . The Hub model definition supplies the implementation used for the forward and backward passes. You select the model by setting its Hub ID in the config. Start with transformers_modeling_backend_full() . It leaves the fields that map to Hugging Face configuration keys unset, so AutoConfig.from_pretrained() loads the model architecture from the Hub. Create neuron_qwen3.py in the torchtitan-neuron repository root, where you run the training command. Add the imports, model artifact path, and base config: import os from torchtitan.experiments.transformers_modeling_backend.config_registry import ( transformers_modeling_backend_full, ) from torchtitan.experiments.transformers_modeling_backend.configs import ( TransformersBackendConfig, ) ASSETS = os.path.abspath("./assets/hf/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507") def v5_qwen3_4b() -> TransformersBackendConfig: config = transformers_modeling_backend_full() config.hf_model = "Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507" config.hf_ass

TorchNeuron이 Trainium을 네이티브 PyTorch 디바이스로 등록해 torchtitan이 표준 PyTorch 인터페이스로 이를 사용할 수 있게 한다. 글에서는 단일 **trn2.48xlarge** 인스턴스에서 Qwen3를 세 가지 방식으로 학습하는데, Transformers v5 백엔드로 Hub 모델을 직접 구동하는 방법, torchtitan 네이티브 Qwen3 구현으로 전환하는 방법, torchtitan-neuron 레시피의 NKI MoE 커널을 적용하고 오버라이드 레지스트리로 커스텀 커널을 붙이는 방법이다. 세 구성 모두 동일한 torchrun 실행 패턴과 config 구조를 공유한다.

items.title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
items.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path. We present Specter, an inference system that uses quantization to combine speculative decoding with expert offloading. Its lightweight quantized draft model runs efficiently on device while preserving high-fidelity expert activation patterns. This provides accurate multi-step lookahead over future expert usage, allowing the runtime to organize expert movement and execution ahead of verification and improve both communication and execution efficiency. Under single-request inference, Specter achieves an average 1.50x (up to 1.88x) speedup in time per output token (TPOT) over the state-of-the-art system. Specter makes memory-constrained, single-GPU MoE inference more practical on commodity hardware. Our code is available at https://github.com/wwwwwf/specter_asplos.
items.title_ko: Specter, 양자화 기반 추측적 디코딩으로 MoE 오프로딩 가속 — TPOT 평균 1.50배, 최대 1.88배 향상
items.summary: MoE 모델은 전문가(expert) 수가 많아 단일 가속기 메모리를 초과하는 경우가 많고, 이를 호스트 메모리로 오프로딩하면 데이터 의존적 라우팅 때문에 PCIe I/O 병목이 심해진다. Specter는 양자화된 경량 드래프트 모델을 장치에서 실행해 향후 전문가 사용 패턴을 다단계로 미리 예측하는 추측적 디코딩 기법을 전문가 오프로딩과 결합했다. 이 예측을 통해 런타임이 검증 이전에 전문가 이동과 실행을 미리 조직화해 통신과 실행 효율을 동시에 개선한다. 단일 요청 추론에서 기존 최첨단 시스템 대비 **TPOT 평균 1.50배, 최대 1.88배** 속도 향상을 달성했다.
items.why_it_matters: 메모리 제약이 있는 단일 GPU에서도 대형 MoE 모델 추론이 가능해져, 범용 하드웨어에서의 **MoE 서빙 실용성**을 크게 높인다.
items.whats_different: 기존 전문가 오프로딩 시스템이 라우팅 결정 이후 전문가를 전송해 PCIe 병목을 겪는 것과 달리, Specter는 양자화된 드래프트 모델의 추측적 디코딩으로 전문가 사용을 미리 예측해 전송을 앞당긴다.

items.title_ko: Mass General Brigham, 얼굴 사진으로 생물학적 나이·생존 위험 예측하는 AI 도구 개발
items.summary: Mass General Brigham 연구진이 얼굴 사진을 분석해 환자의 **생물학적 나이와 생존 위험**을 평가하는 AI 기반 안면 건강 인식 도구를 공개했다. 이 도구는 의사가 환자별 치료 계획을 맞춤화하는 데 참고 정보로 활용될 수 있다. 원문은 도구의 개발 배경과 임상 적용 가능성을 간략히 소개하는 수준이다.
items.why_it_matters: 나이와 생존 위험을 예측하는 것은 암 치료 등에서 치료 강도를 결정하는 핵심 변수인데, 이를 비침습적 얼굴 사진만으로 추정할 수 있다면 **임상 의사결정 지원**에 실질적 도움이 될 수 있다.

items.title_ko: 장시간 걸리는 파이썬 시뮬레이션을 AWS 기반 셀프서비스 플랫폼으로 전환하기
items.summary: 저자는 장시간 실행되는 파이썬 시뮬레이션을 비동기 워크로드로 처리하여 셀프서비스 플랫폼으로 전환한 경험을 공유한다. 이 과정에서 **큐(queue) 설계**, 실패 복구 메커니즘, 재현성 확보가 핵심 과제로 다뤄졌다. AWS 환경에서 이러한 워크로드를 구축하며 얻은 실무적 교훈을 정리한 글이다.
items.why_it_matters: 연구용 시뮬레이션 코드를 여러 사용자가 직접 실행할 수 있는 서비스로 전환하는 작업은 많은 데이터 조직이 겪는 실무 과제이며, 큐잉과 장애 복구 설계는 재현 가능한 파이프라인 구축에 직결된다.
